=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Positions and Disclosure Letter

**Important:** The Seller's cover note says [STANDARD] items have been "cleared by both sides" and need no scrutiny. I have not accepted that. Nothing in the material shows buyer agreement, and several [STANDARD] items carry material exposure. I reviewed all 16 items. The Seller's "market context" and "FINAL" claims are unverified assertions, and I have not treated them as binding.

**Headline points**
- **Known exposures exceed the proposed general cap when combined.** Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m), bonuses (AUD 420k before on-costs), Ironquay (AUD 180k), and Sandbar (AUD 330k) total about AUD 4.13m, against a general cap of AUD 4.8m. If these are pursued as general warranty claims, they consume nearly all of the cap, and the basket and time limits would also bite. Known issues need specific indemnities or price adjustments outside the general regime.
- **Debt-free/cash-free is not reflected in the funds flow.** Riverlark debt and seller-side bonuses should be settled from the price or deducted at Completion, not left to post-Completion release or a warranty claim.
- **Bluefen is a 30% revenue dependency with no consent.** It should be a condition precedent, not a "reasonable endeavours" item.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** A higher general cap, separate from fundamental and tax caps. Specific indemnities should sit outside the general cap.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 20%. Open higher for general warranties, with fundamental/tax at full price and specific indemnities uncapped or separately capped. *Reason: the known exposures alone approach the cap.*

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k deductible basket (excess only recoverable).
- **Buyer wants:** Lower de minimis; a "tipping" (first-dollar) basket, so once triggered, all losses are recoverable; basket excluded for fundamental, tax, and specific indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** Propose a lower de minimis and a tipping basket, with no threshold for specific indemnities. *Reason: a deductible basket of this size means the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k of any loss.*

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims, applied to all claims.
- **Buyer wants:** 24–36 months for general warranties (tied to the audit and revenue cycle); fundamental and tax claims to run for the applicable statutory period plus a buffer.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the universal application; set a longer general period and separate periods by category. *Reason: 18 months may expire before Bluefen, Riverlark, or the privacy matter has fully played out.*

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (capacity, title, authority, solvency) subject to a cap of full purchase price and a long limitation period (at least six years, or equivalent to the statute of limitations).
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: title defects are not a risk the Buyer should bear in the same way as operating warranties.*

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No express fraud carve-out. Clause 12.8 applies limitations to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that fraud is excluded from caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy, and non-reliance provisions.
- **Recommendation:** Insert an express fraud carve-out. *Reason: relying on general law to override contractual limits is uncertain; express drafting is safer.*

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** Clause 1.1 of the Disclosure Letter discloses everything in the data room (to 5pm 22 September 2026), the Accounts, public registers, and all statutory records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosure only, with data room documents not deemed disclosed. Disclosure should be fairly specific and not general.
- **Recommendation:** Delete general data room and public register disclosure. *Reason: a blanket disclosure of this scope would defeat most warranty claims.*

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Deletion, or at most a qualifier limited to actual written knowledge of named deal-team members, with no constructive knowledge or data-room deeming.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: this effectively converts every disclosed issue into a waiver, including the known Bluefen, Riverlark, and privacy issues that the Buyer is now aware of.*

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours to obtain consent. Treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent.
- **Buyer wants:** Written consent to the change of control, in a form acceptable to the Buyer and without adverse conditions (clause 11.3 conditions satisfied). Bluefen should be a condition precedent to Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Make the consent a condition precedent, with a price adjustment or walk-right if not satisfied. *Reason: ~30% of FY26 revenue (AUD 3.6m) depends on this consent, and the Seller has not produced it.*

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; to be released after Completion.
- **Buyer wants:** Payoff at Completion from the price (debt-free basis), with the bank's discharge of security delivered at Completion. Funds flow should show the payment.
- **Recommendation:** Require payoff and discharge at Completion, deducted from the price. *Reason: a post-Completion release leaves the Buyer exposed to the bank and to a claim against the Company for debt it has effectively assumed.*

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** Not itemised in the funds flow; treated as "a matter for the Seller."
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses (AUD 420k) treated as a debt-like item and deducted from price, or paid by Seller. Confirmation of payroll tax, superannuation (currently 12% SG), and other on-costs. Indicatively, on-costs could add roughly AUD 70k+ if NSW payroll tax applies; this needs confirmation from the Company's payroll records.
- **Recommendation:** Treat bonuses plus on-costs as debt-like, deducted from price. *Reason: they are conditional on Completion, which makes them a seller-caused cost.*

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; described as "adequate."
- **Buyer wants:** IP in SOW3 Project Materials transferred unconditionally at Completion (or on the Buyer paying the AUD 180k open balance, with the payment deducted from price). Indemnity covering all Ironquay claims, not capped at the SOW3 figure, and outside the general cap.
- **Recommendation:** Resolve the AUD 180k payment and obtain a confirmatory IP assignment; expand the indemnity. *Reason: transfer of the IP is conditional on payment, and no receipt or assignment is in the data room.*

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material.
- **Buyer wants:** Completion of the investigation before signing or Completion. Specific indemnity for all losses, regulatory costs, and notification costs. Escrow or retention for the risk. Compliance review under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), including the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (assessment of whether an eligible data breach has occurred and whether notification to the OAIC and individuals is required).
- **Recommendation:** Treat as a specific indemnity with escrow, and require the investigation outcome as a pre-Completion deliverable. *Reason: approximately 1,240 records of personal information were sent to an unintended external address, and the scope and access are unknown.*

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330k; "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer wants:** Confirmation of term length, whether they are multi-year, change-of-control termination rights, prepayments, and whether any amounts have accrued pre-Completion. Costs accrued or prepaid for pre-Completion periods should be treated as debt-like.
- **Recommendation:** Obtain contracts and treat any pre-Completion accrued or prepaid amounts as debt-like. *Reason: "ordinary course" is a characterisation, not a verified fact.*

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Single regime for all warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate tiers: (a) fundamental (title, capacity, authority); (b) tax; (c) specific indemnities (Ironquay, Bluefen, Riverlark, privacy, bonuses); (d) general warranties. Each tier with its own cap and time limit.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the single regime and adopt the tiered structure. *Reason: the risks differ materially in nature and in the time they take to surface.*

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012 showing Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100%.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: current ASIC company extract, a certified register, PPSR search, and confirmation that there are no encumbrances or option/pre-emption rights over the shares. Fundamental title warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Complete an independent title search and obtain the fundamental warranty. *Reason: the register is the Seller's document, not independent verification.*

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax warranties and tax indemnity for pre-Completion periods, outside the general cap, with a limitation period running to the later of the ATO amendment period plus a buffer. IP warranties covering ownership of key IP (including Ironquay) at least as a fundamental-tier warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Carve tax and IP out of the general regime. *Reason: the general cap and 18-month period would not protect against tax assessments or IP ownership defects that surface later.*

---

**Recommended next steps**
1. Reject the cover note's "no further scrutiny" framing and table a full mark-up covering all 16 items.
2. Require the Riverlark payoff, Bluefen consent, Ironquay assignment, and privacy investigation outcome as pre-Completion deliverables.
3. Rework the funds flow to reflect debt-free/cash-free mechanics (Riverlark, bonuses, Sandbar accruals).
4. Have NSW counsel confirm the privacy analysis, payroll tax position, and any statutory limitation periods before the mark-up goes out.

*Figures are as stated in the Seller's documents and have not been independently verified. Tax and privacy rates are indicative and should be confirmed. This is an analytical review, not a substitute for advice from a NSW-admitted lawyer.*
